newsitem.title: USA: Alameda Cty, Calif, lessens Grigsby's role in deal.
newsitem.headline: Alameda Cty, Calif, lessens Grigsby's role in deal.

text.p: The Alameda County, Calif., Board of Supervisors on Tuesday voted to remove Calvin Grigsby's investment banking firm from the lead senior underwriter position in an upcoming bond deal.
In a 4-to-0 vote with one abstention, the board selected the firm M.R. Beal & Co to be the lead senior manager for the sale of nearly $300 million of pension obligation bonds.
Grigsby's firm, Grigsby & Associates and Morgan Stanley will serve as co-senior managers for the bond deal.
Grigsby said after the meeting that the decision was fair. "I don't find today's decision objectionable," he said.

Formerly known as Grigsby Brandford & Co, Grigsby's firm has undergone a dramatic shake-up since September, when Grigsby, the firm's founder and long-time chairman, abruptly announced his resignation.
After he left, it was disclosed that authorities were investigating bond deals the firm handled in Dade County, Fla. Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.
Several weeks after he left, Grigsby rejoined his firm, renaming it Grigsby & Associates.
The controversy surrounding Grigsby has taken its toll on his bond business across the country and in Alameda County.
In October, Grigsby was removed as a remarketing agent for commercial paper issued for Alameda County.

Alameda County Administrator Susan Muranishi had recommended that Grigsby's role in the pension bonds be decreased because the county's financial adviser warned "there potentially could be a negative effect on the marketing of the bonds if Grigsby & Associates remains as lead senior manager."

After the vote, Supervisor Ed Campbell, who abstained, said Grigsby should have been completely removed from the bond deal. "There ought to be a clean break when there's a perception of impropriety," he said.
PaineWebber Inc was one of the senior managers before Tuesday's changes. The firm told the county, however, that it did not want to be included as a member of the financing team.

"We will be pleased to serve as your senior book-running manager on this transaction, if you decide to appoint us," PaineWebber told the county in a November 27 letter. "If you decide to choose another firm, we understand that the choice is yours. In that event, we respectfully request that PaineWebber not be included in the transaction."

"This position should not be construed as a reluctance to work with the county," PaineWebber said. "However, the health of the industry and of many firms within the industry has changed dramatically over the past months."
"We are not in the business of guaranteeing the performance of any other person or firm," PaineWebber said.
